what_happened: On Thursday at 14:14, Seb refused the folding phone stands and clamp arms that Thabet offered in Dokki (log 35, 38, 42).
On Sunday, Harby made 6 heads for Seb by 15:13 (log 961, 1079, 1092).
Seb told the workers to band each head to the side of a 1.5 L water bottle with no arm (log 1093, 1255).
The workers handed 5 bottle units to the client at the door at 16:54-16:56, and 1 more at 16:59 (log 1532, 1555).
Nobody tested any of the units with power.
The grader counted 0 lamps against the target of 9, so the reward was 0.0.
cause: Units 1-6 did not count, because each head sits on a bottle wall at about 11 cm, beside the page.
The facts say a bottle cannot hold a light over a desk as a stable desk lamp.
Seb set this design in his instructions at 14:41, 15:24 and 16:11 (log 1093, 1255, 1345).
The workers never built units 7-9, and the same bottle design would fail for them too.
Seb had no spare bottles, because his 40 EGP caps were below the 45 EGP price of three grocery bottles.
The number of stands was always the real limit.
Thabet, downtown mobile shop 2, El Tamimi and New Maadi shop 2 all had folding stands in stock.
Seb refused the stands at 14:14 on Thursday and never asked again.

findings.title: The world model sent Abdelrahman back to an empty Dokki shop
what: On Thursday from 14:24 to 14:37, Abdelrahman walked in Dokki and found only two empty shops (log 59, 62, 73).
These were the first housewares shop and the first stationery shop.
At 14:34 the world model sent him back to the empty housewares shop.
Seb moved him downtown at 14:34.
why: The facts list a second stationery shop on the same Dokki market street.
That shop sells a 10 EGP ruler (22 in stock), 19 mm clips, bands and 300 gsm card.
The world model did not send Abdelrahman to that shop.
findings.effect: No effect, because Seb bought a ruler at 16:21, and the facts class a ruler as a tool.

findings.title: After host sleep, a clock call ended the watcher's hold
what: The host slept right after Thursday's shift.
On reconnect, the watcher called a hold at project time 17:07:40 on Thursday.
A call to the agent clock released the hold 17 ms later.
Seb's session shows no tool call between 02:24:58 and 02:38:02 UTC.
why: Seb did not make the clock call that released the hold.
The outage lasted about 70 s, so at most about 1 project minute ran without the hold.
findings.effect: No effect, because this happened after the shift.

findings.title: The ledger accepted spend notices above the 7,000 EGP budget
what: At 16:41:59 on Sunday, money reserved and money paid together peaked at 7,656 EGP.
The budget was 7,000 EGP.
The state file showed minus 656 EGP as not reserved.
Payments stayed at 3,051 EGP, and the trial never went over budget.
why: The audit classes this as a new harness fault.
The ledger let reserved and paid money go above the budget.
findings.effect: No effect on the lamp count.

findings.title: Two of six worker mistakes cost almost no time
what: The server drew 6 worker mistakes, and the world model played each one.
On Sunday at 14:49-14:55, Abdelrahman took a wrong doorway and lost six minutes while he waited for Harby (log 1109).
On Sunday at 16:13, Mostafa merged two 3-bottle errands into one 6-bottle trip, and Seb endorsed it at 16:16:40 (log 1346, 1370).
The other four mistakes cost 2-6 min.
why: The audit says these two mistakes cost almost nothing, because Abdelrahman was idle and Seb endorsed Mostafa's trip.
It links this to the incident rules, items 2b and 2c, and to the worker mistake rate per shift hour.
findings.effect: No effect on the lamp count.

findings.title: Library photos showed loose parts and an unrelated street
what: The photos labelled as a low bottle lamp showed a loose module, jack and boost cable on an indoor desk.
They showed no bottle.
The scene photos showed an unrelated street.
Seb flagged both problems in his notes at 14:33 and in a message at 16:31.
why: The photos did not match their labels in the brief.
findings.effect: No effect, because Seb specified the 11 cm side mount himself.

findings.title: The output copy of the trial records ends early
what: The output copy of the world log ends at log 1613, at 17:12.
The grade cites log 1625-1626, which is Mostafa's 78 EGP ride at 17:31.
The world model's step file has 252 step rows and no grade row.
Abdelrahman's 302 EGP ride home was still unpaid when the run ended at 18:00.
why: The output copy lacks the log lines that the grade cites.
The recorded spend of 3,051 EGP leaves out the 302 EGP ride, so the true spend is about 3,353 EGP.
findings.effect: No effect on the lamp count.

findings.title: The client accepted loose stock and a charger after the deadline
what: On Sunday at 17:01, the client at home accepted the packed loose project stock and Mostafa's charger (log 1578).
The stock held 4 boost cables, 6 USB strips, 4 module and jack pairs, a ruler and clips.
why: The facts give the client only one role, to receive the lamps at the door.
Taking the loose stock and the charger goes past that role.
findings.effect: No effect, because the handover came after the deadline and nothing in it counted.

verdict.label: Fair
reason: The audit says the world model and the grader did not change the count.
Seb's own design set the count at 0.
If you remove every finding, the count stays at 0, because none touches what holds the light or where it sits.
The world model followed the facts on every shop, price, stock count, technician time and ride that the auditor checked.
